reviewer: Claude review of the divided source object’s label and the requirement leaves; not a radiologist review
decision: Bind the two duct parts of BodyParts3D 4.3 object FJ3079. Requested by the project owner on 2026-11-24. One part binds under the rules of the body-reader pass; the other does not.
rule: A label mesh is recorded and bound when the reader that shows it is shown in the requirement’s investigation, its own source label names the requirement (own words, another name, or one member of a group), the leaf is the structure itself, the part the label names, the structure’s own body, or one member of a named group, the requirement is anatomy and not an example of pathology, a lumen leaf comes from a source that segments the opacified lumen, the source’s population fits the investigation, the object lies where its label says and is no wider than its label, and a stated side agrees with the requirement and with where the decoded mesh lies: a body side against the source midline and the mirror mesh, an organ half against its named partner. A whole is not bound to its parts, and a part is not bound to its whole. Coverage is always partial.

bodyparts3d.shown_by: The 3D tab shows the BodyParts3D region named by the investigation’s spatial-model family (web/radiology-detailed-anatomy.js ALIASES map heart to coronary and kidney to renal) when the investigation has no source anatomy reference of its own; ra.brain-anatomy names the BodyParts3D brain as its whole-brain context reference. The prostate investigation has its own source reference, so no investigation shows the prostate region.

bodyparts3d.why: BodyParts3D axes in millimetres with Z up. The liver’s right lobe (hepatovenous segments V to VIII) and the gallbladder lie at -X, and the ventricular wall and the circumflex artery at +X, so -X is the body’s right. The third and fourth ventricles and the prostate mark the midline from head to pelvis. The BodyParts3D 4.3 readers (biliary, dural, cardiac, thoracic) use the same coordinates: their gallbladder and atrial-wall meshes have exactly the centroids of the 4.0 meshes with the same identifiers.
